extensions.name: agent-civilization
extensions.title: Agent Civilization
extensions.description: Agent Civilization: every agent at work as a living pixel-art town, with the files, shells, sites, models, MCP servers, and messages they share, and every task as a building that its own work puts up. It watches the tool calls and messages of every session, shows the owner only the sessions that Pi Pocket confirms they may see, and keeps a short history in its own data folder. No network.

extensions.name: agent-recipes
extensions.title: Agent recipes
extensions.description: Author recipe drafts in conversation, share owner-accepted snapshots, and start linked roles after owner confirmation or under a bounded conversation policy. Automatic use and status use experimental host-linked APIs; automatic use acts as the current source requester, not the authorizing owner. Reads only module documents, source settings and model metadata; no outside files or secrets, direct external network calls, or processes. Linked agents use normal tools and providers; work modes are instructions, not a sandbox.

extensions.name: blueprint
extensions.title: Blueprint
extensions.description: A drafting table: cyanotype blue on a faint grid, square ink lines, crop-marked cards, and mono labels. Its light half is a whiteprint.

extensions.name: browser-runs
extensions.title: Browser runs
extensions.description: Browser runs: Pi gives the browser one goal and the values it may type, and a run model carries it out a step at a time, without Pi: it clicks and types without asking, on the session's page, which may be signed in, so a hostile page can steer it. The run model is the owner's choice: the session's own model, or Jev on OpenRouter (openrouter.ai), which then gets each step's goal, supplied values, page address, title and text (up to 4,000 characters), controls in view with their values, and recent actions, with the owner's OpenRouter key.

extensions.name: browser-sign-in
extensions.title: Browser sign-in
extensions.description: Browser sign-in: when Pi's browser is at a sign-in, the person types the username and password, or a one-time code, on a card in the chat, and the values go straight into the page. Pi never sees them, and neither does the transcript. For a CAPTCHA or a sign-in to approve on a phone, Pi asks the person to do it in the Browser panel and tap Done.

extensions.name: change-atlas
extensions.title: Change Atlas
extensions.description: Change Atlas: Pi maps a pull request, branch, commit range, or local changes into an interactive visual report. It reads a git repository (the session's folder, or the folder that Pi names) with `git` (for a pull request also `gh` and `git fetch`, which contact GitHub), and writes reports and fetched PR commits to `change-atlas/` in the data folder. Diff excerpts go to the model provider, and a published report goes to everyone who sees the session. It sends nothing to any other host.

extensions.name: charm-hyper
extensions.title: Charm Hyper
extensions.description: Charm Hyper: adds Charm's Hyper models to Pi Pocket. It reads the hyper API key from Pi's sign-ins, sends it only to hyper.charm.land, and refreshes the model catalog from Hyper.

extensions.name: claude-code
extensions.title: Claude Code
extensions.description: Claude's desktop app: serif replies, your messages as bubbles on the right, a flat sidebar, and a rounded reply box. Pi keeps its own π.

extensions.name: decision-notebook
extensions.title: Decision notebook
extensions.description: Keep conversation decisions with Pi proposals and direct owner review, acceptance, and supersession. Uses only this module's Durable documents and public Pocket APIs; no outside files, secrets, processes, or network services.

extensions.name: donsetch
extensions.title: DonSeTch for Pi Pocket
extensions.description: DonSeTch web fetch, search, crawl, and screenshot tools for Pi Pocket, through the local donsetch MCP binary. The module starts that binary on the first tool call in each conversation with a limited environment. The binary contacts the URLs you request and the third-party search engines and sources used by web_search, including Google, Bing, Brave, DuckDuckGo, Yahoo, Mojeek, GitHub, Wikipedia, Hacker News, Semantic Scholar, arXiv, Stack Exchange, MDN, and Google News. See the donsetch documentation for the current providers.

extensions.name: keenable
extensions.title: Keenable web search
extensions.description: Keenable web search for Pi: keenable_search finds web pages, and keenable_fetch reads a public page as markdown. Each call sends the query, or the page's address, to api.keenable.ai with the header X-Keenable-Title: Pi Pocket. It needs no key. An optional Keenable API key in the module's settings raises the rate limits; it stays on the server and goes only to api.keenable.ai. Results are fenced as data from the web. The module reads no other files, settings, or secrets.

extensions.name: mcp
extensions.title: MCP servers
extensions.description: MCP servers for Pi: Pi Pocket connects to the stdio and HTTP servers in Pi's own mcp.json, and Pi finds and calls their tools with mcp_tools, mcp_call, and mcp_call_read_only. Each server is a program that runs with the owner's rights, and Lancet Guard does not check the calls of its tools. A server runs only after the owner turns it on in the MCP page, and again after each change to its entry. The module reads ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json and the variables and commands that its entries name, and keeps its settings and OAuth tokens in ~/.pi-pocket/mcp/.

extensions.name: personas
extensions.title: Pi Pocket Personas
extensions.description: Personas are saved system-prompt instructions for Pi Pocket. Choose one for a session — a terse reviewer, a patient teacher, a teammate who follows your house rules — and Pi follows it from the next request. Edit them on a page, pick one from the message box or status line, and set a default for new sessions. A session can have one, or none; the text is added to Pi's system prompt for that session only.

extensions.name: pink-sakura
extensions.title: Pink Sakura
extensions.description: Light Pink with a seamless 1024 px sakura wallpaper: pale blossoms tile in the gaps between the tiled windows and show through them.

extensions.name: ponytail
extensions.title: Ponytail
extensions.description: Ponytail provides mode guidance, session controls, and conservative verification reminders; it never runs or blocks commands.

extensions.name: project-workbench
extensions.title: Project workbench
extensions.description: An owner-only project workbench: reads the bound session's package.json and Git metadata, runs Git status/worktree queries, and starts npm scripts only after owner confirmation. Scripts and npm may read files, secrets, environment variables and network services with the server user's rights. Stores preview settings in a namespaced document and bounded run results under the data folder. Preview links are user-entered loopback HTTP(S); no service discovery or external requests by the extension.

extensions.name: secrets
extensions.title: Secrets
extensions.description: Secrets: API keys and tokens that Pi uses without seeing them. The owner keeps them in Menu → Secrets; a bash command that names one ($NPM_TOKEN) runs with its value, and output that shows a value shows [secret NPM_TOKEN] instead. Pi can list them, ask the owner for one on a card with a hidden field, and keep a command's output as one.

extensions.name: subscription-usage
extensions.title: Subscription usage
extensions.description: Subscription usage: a page on the rail with how much of your Claude, ChatGPT (Codex), OpenCode Go, Grok, Z.ai, and MiniMax plans is used, and when each limit resets, plus the DeepSeek balance, a status line item with the quota of the open session's model provider, and a /usage-plans command that posts the same usage as a card in chat. The server asks each service with the sign-ins already on this machine, and sends each key only to its own service (anthropic.com, opencode.ai, grok.com, z.ai, minimax.io, deepseek.com). No key or token reaches the browser.

extensions.name: update-notifier
extensions.title: Pocket updates
extensions.description: Notify the owner when a newer stable Pi Pocket release is available. Compares the running server version with the fixed public GitHub release API. Checks while an owner has Pocket open, caches results and rate-limit waits, and supports manual checks and dismissal. Uses only its own durable documents. Sends no credentials or user content. Does not install updates, run Git, restart Pocket, or call a model.

extensions.name: usage-analyser
extensions.title: Usage analyser (experimental)
extensions.description: Usage analyser (experimental): token, cost, cache and time findings; ideas for other analyses are welcome. An owner-only page runs a child process that reads Pi Pocket records, never keeps or shows message text, and stores a cache in <data>/usage-analyser/. Ask PiP sends findings to PiP. sessions() is experimental; /pip.js and the pocket.sqlite record shapes are internal and can change in any release. The analyser makes no network requests; PiP may send findings to its model provider.

extensions.name: voice-message
extensions.title: Voice message
extensions.description: Dictate a message: words appear while you speak and a full pass corrects them when you stop; nothing is sent automatically and your edits are never overwritten. Mistral engines send audio to api.mistral.ai (Voxtral Realtime 3, then Mini Transcribe 3; key only on the server from MISTRAL_API_KEY or Pi's mistral auth.json entry). Local Whisper keeps audio on the server; its first use installs pinned packages from PyPI with enforced hashes and the revision-pinned Whisper small model from huggingface.co, ~900 MB. Engine and language (auto by default) are chosen on the Audio settings page.
